combinations.name: MAOIs
combinations.description: Phenelzine, tranylcypromine, selegiline, etc. — MAO inhibition removes the main breakdown route for released monoamines, so pressor effects stack into hypertensive crisis. With methamphetamine's potency and duration the margin is even thinner than with amphetamine. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Alcohol
combinations.description: The stimulant masks how drunk you are, so alcohol tends to get redosed well past where it would alone — and methamphetamine's long duration means the masking outlasts most drinking sessions. Cardiovascular load adds up; judgment of it does not.

combinations.name: Other stimulants
combinations.description: Cocaine, MDMA, more amphetamine — heart rate and blood pressure effects are additive, and methamphetamine already sits at the strong end. Stacking raises cardiovascular load faster than it raises the effect you wanted.

combinations.name: Opioids
combinations.description: The stimulant masks opioid sedation, the usual early warning of too much — so an opioid dose that would have felt heavy feels manageable until the stimulant wears off first. If combining, dose the opioid as if the stimulant weren't there.

waterHeat.headline: Sip to thirst
waterHeat.body: Stimulants suppress thirst without changing how much fluid you actually need — which isn't much more than usual unless you're moving hard or in the heat. Sip to thirst rather than forcing water, and over a long session remember to eat; hours pass faster than they feel.
